summary: Target-level continuation of the accepted V.2 plan. Import the graded comparison and the general Bass–Tate theorem from their Milnor-K owner; supply real-place representatives, the product identity, decomposable signatures and natural quotient equivalences. The integral injectivity proof has an explicit source-based supplier contract. This is a completed planning pass, with foundational supplier refinements recorded rather than a claim of formalisation or gap-free closure.

nodes.title: Real-place basis of Milnor K₃
nodes.statement: Let R(F) be the finite subtype of real infinite places and σ_F:K₃ᴹ(F)≃⊕_{v∈R(F)} Z/2 the imported Bass–Tate signature, written additively with 1 for an all-negative triple. Define b_v=σ_F⁻¹(δ_v), where δ_v is 1 at v and 0 elsewhere. This is canonical; choosing a sign-isolating unit is not part of its data.
proofSteps: Use the supplier isomorphism, not a fresh presentation of Milnor K-theory.
Transport the coordinate generators and their finite expansion through σ_F.
Naturality of signatures transports restriction: a basis class at v maps to the sum of basis classes over real places lying above v. If no real place lies above v the sum is zero.
acceptance: For Q the unique generator is {−1,−1,−1}.
An empty real-place type gives the zero group.
Distinct coordinates give distinct nonzero elements of order two.

sources.locator: Chapter II §2, Theorem (2.1)(3), printed p.396; final proof paragraph, printed p.402 (volume PDF pp.406,412).
sources.match: The sign-isolating generators and their order-two section in the final proof paragraph give the imported signature coordinates. This node canonically transports those coordinates through the supplier isomorphism.

api.name: realBasis_signature
api.statement: σ_F(b_v)(w) equals 1 if w=v and 0 otherwise.

api.name: realBasis_nonzero
api.statement: b_v≠0 for each real place v.

api.name: realBasis_expand
api.statement: Every x is the sum of b_v over the real places with σ_F(x)(v)=1.

api.name: realBasis_map
api.statement: For an embedding F→L of number fields, restriction sends b_v to the sum over real places w of L restricting to v.

tests.name: realBasis_single
tests.statement: With the single real coordinate of Q, σ_Q(b)=1.

tests.name: realBasis_empty
tests.statement: When R(F) is empty every x∈K₃ᴹ(F) equals zero.

tests.name: realBasis_distinct
tests.statement: For two distinct real places v,w, b_v≠b_w. Defining every generator as {−1,−1,−1} fails this test.

uses.how: Canonicalise the sign-isolating generators used in the proof.
Keep the real signature contribution visible in the integral K₃ input.
Track the separate real-place decomposable classes.

nodes.title: Symbol representatives of the real-place basis
nodes.statement: For each real place v of a number field F, there exists u_v∈F× negative at v and positive at every other real place. For every such u_v, b_v={−1,−1,u_v}. Thus the symbol is independent of the chosen sign-isolating unit.
proofSteps: Use weak approximation on a nonempty open sign box, including arbitrary open constraints at the complex places. The chosen element is nonzero because it has negative value at v.
Evaluate {−1,−1,u_v} under σ_F: it has exactly the v coordinate equal to 1.
Apply injectivity of σ_F. Alternatively Bass–Tate rewrites {u_v,u_v,u_v} as {−1,−1,u_v} using the Milnor repeated-entry identity.
acceptance: For Q choose u=−1.
Changing u without changing its signs does not change the class.

sources.locator: Chapter II §2, Theorem (2.1)(3), printed p.396; final proof paragraph, printed p.402 (volume PDF pp.406,412).
sources.match: The proof chooses a unit negative at exactly one real place and rewrites its third power as the ordered symbol {−1,−1,u_v}. Weak approximation and signature injectivity give the stated representative and choice independence.

nodes.title: Surjectivity of the product with −1
nodes.statement: For a number field F the additive homomorphism p_F:K₂ᴹ(F)→K₃ᴹ(F), x↦{−1}·x, is surjective. Under Matsumoto and the imported graded comparison, the image of K₂(F) --[−1]·→ K₃(F) equals the decomposable subgroup D(F)=im(m₃). This statement is about number fields; no all-fields equality of these two images is asserted.
proofSteps: Each b_v has preimage {−1,u_v} under p_F. Finite coordinate expansion therefore proves surjectivity.
The natural product square p_F,m₂,m₃ and [−1]· commutes by the graded comparison, with m₂ an isomorphism. Equality of images follows.
Combining with the inherited stable Hurewicz kernel identifies that kernel with D(F).
acceptance: For Q the all-minus-one triple is in the image.
For a totally imaginary number field both images are zero.
No Quillen K₃ order calculation is used to prove surjectivity.

sources.locator: Chapter II §2, Theorem (2.1)(3), printed p.396; final proof paragraph, printed p.402 (volume PDF pp.406,412).
sources.match: Each real coordinate is represented by {−1,−1,u_v}, hence lifts from {−1,u_v} in Milnor K₂. Surjectivity and the Quillen image identity are consumer consequences using Matsumoto and the graded supplier, rather than additional assertions of Bass–Tate.

nodes.title: Signature of the decomposable subgroup
nodes.statement: For a number field F, let D(F)=im(m₃)⊆K₃(F), the inherited decomposable subgroup. Integral injectivity gives j:K₃ᴹ(F)≃D(F). Construct s_D:D(F)≃⊕_{v real} Z/2 as σ_F∘j⁻¹. In particular |D(F)|=2^{r₁} and every element of D(F) is killed by 2; do not identify D(F) with all torsion in K₃(F).
proofSteps: Use injectivity to corestrict m₃ to an isomorphism onto its actual range.
Compose its inverse with the supplier signature isomorphism.
Count the finite product and transport exponent two; functoriality is the naturality of m₃ and signatures.
acceptance: D(Q) has two elements; its nonzero element is m₃{−1,−1,−1}.
If r₁=0 then D(F)=0.
The inclusion D(F)⊆torsion(K₃(F)) need not be equality.

sources.match: The integral degree-three Milnor-to-Quillen map is injective. Transport through its corestriction to the image combines this theorem with the independent Bass–Tate signature; no identification with all torsion is made.

sources.locator: Chapter II §2, Theorem (2.1)(3), printed p.396; final proof paragraph, printed p.402 (volume PDF pp.406,412).
sources.match: The imported Bass–Tate signature identifies Milnor K₃ with the finite real-coordinate product; integral injectivity then transports it to the actual image subgroup.

api.name: decomposableSignature_symm
api.statement: s_D⁻¹(t) has ambient K₃ class m₃(σ_F⁻¹(t)).

api.name: decomposableSignature_card
api.statement: The finite cardinality of D(F) equals 2^{r₁}.

api.name: decomposableSignature_map
api.statement: Restriction of D(F)→D(L) corresponds to pulling back sign functions along R(L)→R(F).

tests.name: decomposableSignature_zero
tests.statement: The signature of m₃(0) is the zero function.

tests.name: decomposableSignature_one_real
tests.statement: A class mapping to the unique coordinate 1 is nonzero, so D(Q) is not zero.

tests.name: decomposableSignature_empty
tests.statement: With an empty real-place type every ambient decomposable class is zero.

tests.name: decomposableSignature_coordinate
tests.statement: For every real place v, the decomposable signature of the ambient Milnor image m₃(b_v) is δ_v. Postcomposing with a nontrivial coordinate permutation or another additive automorphism fails this test.

uses.how: Specify the actual embedded real-place subgroup before computing the quotient.
Separate real-place 2-torsion from the remaining torsion and free parts.

nodes.title: Indecomposable quotient for totally imaginary number fields
nodes.statement: If F is a number field with r₁=0, the inherited quotient q_F:K₃(F)→K₃^ind(F) is an additive equivalence e_F. Construct it from q_F and D(F)=0; its inverse is the unique lift of a quotient class. It is natural for embeddings between totally imaginary number fields.
hypotheses: F has no real infinite places: r₁(F)=0.
proofSteps: The supplier Bass–Tate signature makes K₃ᴹ(F)=0, hence the image subgroup is zero.
The quotient map is surjective and has zero kernel, hence bijective.
Use uniqueness of the inverse to prove its evaluation, inverse laws and naturality.
acceptance: The result applies to Q(i), independently of the later calculation of its K₃.
It cannot be applied to Q, whose decomposable subgroup is nonzero.

sources.locator: Chapter II §2, Theorem (2.1)(3), printed p.396; final proof paragraph, printed p.402 (volume PDF pp.406,412).
sources.match: The real-coordinate product is zero when r₁=0, so Milnor K₃ and its image vanish. The equivalence of the quotient map is the resulting elementary quotient consequence.

sources.locator: VI.5 opening, chapter PDF p.23 (definition of the cokernel).
sources.match: K₃^ind is defined as the cokernel of the Milnor comparison. With the Bass–Tate zero source for r₁=0, the quotient map itself is an equivalence; its construction requires no numerical torsion computation.

api.name: totallyImaginaryQuotientEquiv_map
api.statement: For an embedding of totally imaginary number fields, e_L∘K₃(f)=K₃^ind(f)∘e_F.

tests.name: totallyImaginaryQuotient_zero
tests.statement: The equivalence takes zero to the zero quotient class.

tests.name: totallyImaginaryQuotient_representative
tests.statement: Applying the inverse to the quotient class of x recovers x.

uses.how: Pass the integral K₃ structure to the indecomposable quotient with the canonical map.
Use integral K₃ directly when there are no real places.

nodes.title: Stable homology and indecomposable K₃ of a number field
nodes.statement: For a number field F the inherited stable Hurewicz map h_F:K₃(F)→H₃(SL(F),Z) factors uniquely through an additive equivalence e_h:K₃^ind(F)≃H₃(SL(F),Z). Here SL(F) is the stable special linear group, not SL₂(F). The equivalence is natural under embeddings of number fields.
proofSteps: The inherited Hurewicz map is surjective, with kernel im(m₃∘p_F).
The product theorem makes that kernel D(F).
Apply the baseline quotient equivalence with its evaluation on representatives; naturality follows from surjectivity of q_F.
acceptance: h_F kills every decomposable class.
For a totally imaginary number field, h_F itself is an isomorphism.
This conclusion does not identify unstable H₃(SL₂(F),Z) with K₃^ind(F).

sources.locator: Chapter II §2, Theorem (2.1)(3), printed p.396; final proof paragraph, printed p.402 (volume PDF pp.406,412).
sources.match: The sign-isolating representatives yield the preceding product-surjectivity theorem. Combining that theorem with the stable Hurewicz kernel gives this quotient consequence.

sources.locator: VI.5 opening paragraph, chapter PDF p.23.
sources.match: The stable Hurewicz map is surjective with kernel the image of {−1}·K₂ᴹ. The preceding number-field product-surjectivity theorem turns that image into D(F), so the quotient universal property gives the equivalence.

api.name: stableHurewiczQuotientEquiv_unique
api.statement: Every additive homomorphism with this evaluation on q_F equals e_h.

api.name: stableHurewiczQuotientEquiv_map
api.statement: e_h commutes with K₃^ind(f) and stable H₃(SL(f),Z).

tests.name: stableHurewiczQuotient_zero
tests.statement: The equivalence sends the zero class to zero.

tests.name: stableHurewiczQuotient_decomposable
tests.statement: e_h(q_F(m₃(x)))=0 for every Milnor class x.

tests.name: stableHurewiczQuotient_representative
tests.statement: For every ambient class x, e_h(q_F(x))=h_F(x). An unrelated isomorphism with the same kernel or a postcomposition by an automorphism of stable H₃ fails this test.

nodes.title: Vanishing of the integral weight-two mod-two obstruction
nodes.statement: For every field F of characteristic different from 2, H⁰(F,Z(2))/2=0. Consequently the integral differential d₂:H⁰(F,Z(2))→K₃ᴹ(F) in the inherited low-degree sequence is zero. This theorem refines the characteristic-not-two branch of the inherited injectivity proof; it does not use that injectivity theorem as an input.
proofSteps: The exponent-two kernel bound makes d₂ factor through H(F)=H⁰(F,Z(2))/2.

The coefficient exact sequence injects H(F) into H⁰(F,Z/2(2)). The natural motivic-to-étale comparison in degree zero, weight two identifies the latter with H⁰_et(F,μ₂⊗²)=Z/2. The map on these constant groups for F→Fbar is the identity, hence H(F)→H(Fbar) is injective.

Over Fbar, Milnor K₃ is uniquely divisible, hence has no 2-torsion. The exponent-two bound first forces d₂=0 there. Exactness then makes K₄(Fbar)→H⁰(Fbar,Z(2)) surjective. Divisibility of K₄ therefore makes H⁰ divisible. Thus H(Fbar)=0 and H(F)=0.

Use the corrected characteristic scope of the divisibility supplier: VI.1.6 in characteristic zero; VI.1.3.1(i) in positive characteristic. Do not use rational Chern characters to deduce the integral exponent-two bound.
acceptance: The argument applies to Q and to fields of odd positive characteristic.
Characteristic two instead requires Izhboldin’s no-2-torsion theorem and the inherited kernel bound.
The coefficient spectral-sequence differential may still be nonzero.

sources.locator: VI.4.3.1–4.3.2, chapter PDF pp.17–18; for the corrected K₄-divisibility citation, VI.1.3.1(i), p.3, and VI.1.6(i), pp.4–5.
sources.match: Read the low-degree row and the characteristic-not-two proof of integral injectivity. The new node isolates the H⁰(Z(2))/2 vanishing step, with natural restriction, the exponent-two bound, and both characteristic cases of K₄ divisibility; it does not assume the final injectivity theorem.
With the diagonal Milnor identification the Chern composite in degree three is multiplication by +2. Construction of the integral Chern classes is a supplier extension, not a new object of V.2.

nodes.title: Motivic edge description of indecomposable K₃
nodes.statement: For every field F the edge map e_F:K₃(F)→H¹(F,Z(2)) in the inherited low-degree integral sequence induces a natural additive equivalence e_m:K₃^ind(F)≃H¹(F,Z(2)), characterized by e_m(q_F(x))=e_F(x). This is a quotient assertion; it uses right exactness of the sequence and does not need injectivity of m₃.
proofSteps: Right exactness identifies ker(e_F)=D(F) and gives surjectivity of the edge map.
Apply QuotientAddGroup.liftEquiv; prove uniqueness by surjectivity of q_F.
Use naturality of the low-degree sequence to prove the field-map square.
acceptance: The equivalence kills all Milnor images.
Its domain is the quotient rather than the full K₃ group.
It is integral, not an equivalence only after rationalisation.

sources.match: The integral low-degree sequence is right exact at K₃ and H¹(Z(2)). Surjectivity and equality of the edge kernel with the actual Milnor image suffice for the quotient equivalence, independently of injectivity of m₃.

api.name: motivicEdgeQuotientEquiv_unique
api.statement: Every additive homomorphism with this evaluation on representatives equals e_m.

api.name: motivicEdgeQuotientEquiv_map
api.statement: The equivalence commutes with maps induced by every field homomorphism.

tests.name: motivicEdgeQuotient_zero
tests.statement: The equivalence takes the zero quotient class to zero.

tests.name: motivicEdgeQuotient_symbol
tests.statement: e_m(q_F(m₃(x)))=0 for every Milnor class x.

tests.name: motivicEdgeQuotient_lift
tests.statement: The inverse of the edge image e_F(x) is exactly q_F(x).

This supplier gives the filtered K-theory mechanism; the V.2 low-degree extraction remains the inherited consumer lemma.

Keep finiteness from II §1, the prime-to-p restriction/transfer, norm-residue/Hasse-Brauer injection, Hilbert reciprocity, idelic orthogonality, and Kummer weak-approximation inputs owned by their proper suppliers; M.2 local/global and real-place duality and T.7 Hilbert-symbol inputs must not be replaced by an unsupported cardinality argument. The V.2 consumer is not an incoming prerequisite of the general theorem.

Resolve the supplier’s algebraically-closed Milnor divisibility proof gap: K_nᴹ(Fbar) uniquely divisible for n≥2, in particular n=3, with the degree restriction and characteristic-prime case explicit. The statement exists and is imported exactly; proof closure remains at the supplier.

Part II in the Milnor-theory direction: Izhboldin’s theorem, K_nᴹ(F) has no p-torsion for char(F)=p, n≥1. Read K-book III.7.8 including its Bloch–Kato–Gabber, transfer and induction inputs. Degree-three characteristic-two application belongs to V.2, while the general theorem and proof belong to this supplier. This request is an extension beyond the current symbols stage and remains gap G-Izhboldin.
Finite generation of K₃(O_F), not merely finite rank or finite generation after tensoring with Q.
Apply Borel’s independent rank theorem to K₃(O_F), with rank r₂. Export this via N.5 to K₃(F), rather than constructing a second Borel regulator/rank theorem in V.2.

The canonical localization isomorphism K₃(O_F)→K₃(F), and the S-integer variant, with maps. This alone, together with N.3, is the arithmetic input for V.2; no need to import the downstream V.5 or N.8 rational-number order computations.

gaps.title: Foundational integral motivic Chern construction needs its own supplier extension
gaps.detail: The V.11.11 construction uses motivic cohomology on simplicial B•GL, the projective-bundle theorem, localization and Whitney/splitting formulas. V.11.3 then produces natural higher operations c_{i,n}; V.11.13 gives c_{i,i}∘m_i=(-1)^{i−1}(i−1)!id, hence c_{3,3}∘m₃=+2id. The passages and proofs were read; Bloch [Bl86], MVW projective-bundle/localization foundations and the product-rule exercise were not independently decomposed. No existing fine node supplies the integral construction. Route it to MotivicEtaleKTheory, Part II over M.4/M.6 and the higher-Chern direction of SchemeKTheory S.7. Do not use regulator stage M.8: its V.4 dependency would create a backedge. The inherited kernel-exponent-two theorem remains conditional on this supplier refinement. The author-copy localization display requires the first projective bundle to be P(F′), as recorded in E31; the Gysin weight n′ is already correct.

gaps.title: General characteristic-prime Milnor torsion theorem lacks a fine owner node
gaps.detail: K-book III.7.8 and its proof were read. The proof uses the differential-symbol injection III.7.7.2, p-divisibility of the p-torsion subgroup from Bloch–Kato [2.8], Artin–Schreier extension transfer, and the inductive P(E)=I(E) auxiliary result III.7.8.2. These underlying primary papers were not obtained/read in this pass. The theorem is a Milnor-theory Part II request, not a new V.2 theorem or an assertion that M.5d already states it. Once supplied, the inherited exponent-two bound kills the degree-three kernel in characteristic two.

gaps.title: Degree-zero motivic comparison and algebraically-closed divisibility are requested extensions
gaps.detail: M.5 currently states the diagonal norm-residue isomorphism; it does not by itself identify H⁰(F,Z/2(2)) with étale H⁰. M.7 has rigidity/comparison scope but no inspected fine K₄-divisibility node. The exact statements and characteristic restrictions are in the requests. The V.2 obstruction proof records the natural constant-group restriction needed for its descent step. This prevents treating an injection into Z/2 as an unsupported injection into the algebraic closure group.

gaps.title: Inherited Milnor supplier proof gaps remain with their owners
gaps.detail: The general Bass–Tate and algebraically closed Milnor theorem nodes exist and are imported without duplication. Their supplier packet records proof gaps. BT1973 II §2 now gives the original proof and the sign-basis representatives; II §§3–5 and the cited Moore/Tate/Weil proofs were not read, so the general theorem is not certified source-decomposed by this consumer job. The algebraically closed unique-divisibility input is imported in the valid range n≥2. Refine both supplier proofs rather than copy them into V.2.

sourceIssues.reason: The coefficient triangle raises cohomological degree by one. Divisibility of H⁰(F,Z(2)) removes the preceding cokernel H⁰/m, giving an isomorphism H⁰(F,μ_m⊗²)≅H¹(F,Z(2))[m]. imports.provides: Specialise the graded ring map K^M_*(F) -> K_*(F) imported from K2SymbolsBrauer T.2:graded-map to degree three, obtaining a homomorphism K_3^M(F) -> K_3(F) determined by the product of three units. Nothing about this map is asserted in degrees other than three, and its degree-two case, an isomorphism by Matsumoto's theorem, is not a model for degree three.

Define K_3^ind(F) as the cokernel of the degree-three Milnor-to-Quillen map, together with the quotient map K_3(F) -> K_3^ind(F). The decomposable part is by definition the image of that map; it is a subgroup of K_3(F) isomorphic to K_3^M(F) only once injectivity has been proved, which is a separate theorem.
The sequence K_3^M(F) -> K_3(F) -> K_3^ind(F) -> 0 is exact and natural in F. Exactness on the left is not asserted here; it is the content of the injectivity theorem.
For every field F the degree-three map K_3^M(F) -> K_3(F) is injective. Consequently the decomposable part is isomorphic to K_3^M(F) and the sequence of the previous lemma is short exact.

For a number field F with r_1 real places, the signature map K_3^M(F) → ⊕_{v real} K_3^M(F_v)_tors ≅ (Z/2)^{r_1}, sending {a,b,c} to −1 at v exactly when a, b and c are all negative at v (K-book III.7.2(c)), is an isomorphism. In particular K_3^M(F) is torsion, is detected at the real places, and vanishes exactly when F is totally imaginary.

For a number field F, K_3(F) is finitely generated and its free rank is r_2, the number of complex places. The same holds for the indecomposable quotient, since the kernel of the quotient map is torsion by the previous node.
For a number field F, the quotient map induces an isomorphism K_3(F) ⊗_Z Q ≅ K_3^ind(F) ⊗_Z Q of rational vector spaces of dimension r_2, and K_3^M(F) ⊗_Z Q = 0.

For a field F, the Hurewicz map K_3(F) → H_3(SL(F), Z) is surjective, and its kernel is the image under milnorToQuillen3 of the subgroup {−1}·K_2^M(F) of K_3^M(F) generated by the symbols {−1, a, b}. Once V.2/milnor-k3-injective is available, the kernel is that subgroup itself.

For a field k, the motivic spectral sequence E_2^{p,q} = H^{p−q}(k, Z(−q)) ⇒ K_{−p−q}(k) yields an exact sequence K_4(k) → H^0(k, Z(2)) → K_3^M(k) → K_3(k) → H^1(k, Z(2)) → 0, in which the middle map is milnorToQuillen3 under the Nesterenko–Suslin–Totaro isomorphism K_3^M(k) ≅ H^3(k, Z(3)), and the map into K_3^M(k) is the differential d_2.
For every field F, twice every element of the kernel of K_3^M(F) → K_3(F) is zero.

sourceAudit.bassTateProof: Finite generation, reduction modulo primes and prime-to-p extension, norm-residue reciprocity/injectivity and the idelic character argument leave only real signatures. The sign-isolating x_v={u_v,…,u_v}={−1,…,−1,u_v} have order two and give a section; finite generation and the modulo-prime calculation force the remaining subgroup to vanish. This audit records the source route without re-owning its general theorem.
